60:## server.port [​](https://vite.dev/config/server-options\#server-port)
61-
62-- **Type:**`number`
63-- **Default:**`5173`
64-
65:Specify server port. Note if the port is already being used, Vite will automatically try the next available port so this may not be the actual port the server ends up listening on.
66-
67-## server.strictPort [​](https://vite.dev/config/server-options\#server-strictport)
68-
69-- **Type:**`boolean`
70-
71-Set to `true` to exit if port is already in use, instead of automatically trying the next available port.

203-- `protocol` \- WebSocket protocol (`ws` or `wss`)
204-- `host` \- WebSocket server host
205:- `port` \- WebSocket server port
206-- `path` \- WebSocket path
207-- `clientPort` \- Override the port on the client side, allowing you to serve the websocket on a different port than the client code looks for it on
208-- `timeout` \- Connection timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000)
209-- `server` \- Use a custom HTTP server for WebSocket connections
210-
211-When `server.ws.server` is defined, Vite will process the WebSocket connection requests through the provided server. If not in middleware mode, Vite will attempt to process WebSocket connection requests through the existing server. This can be helpful when using self-signed certificates or when you want to expose Vite over a network on a single port.

246-- **Default:** auto (`true` when an AI coding agent is detected based on [`@vercel/detect-agent`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@vercel/detect-agent), otherwise `false`)

content.text:
According to the Vite docs (`server.port` in the server options), the default port is **5173**.

If that port is already in use, Vite tries the next available port. To make it exit instead, set `server.strictPort: true`.

Source: https://vite.dev/config/server-options
